I hit the same problem — my DB was 1.3 GB with 56% freelist pages (only 525 MB of live data). I built a small tool to handle the cleanup safely:

 - pip install ocdbc
 - ocdbc analyze   # read-only health report
 - ocdbc vacuum    # safe cleanup with backup + integrity checks

It checkpoints WAL, verifies integrity before and after, creates a timestamped backup, enables `auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL`, runs VACUUM with progress, and re-enables WAL. Refuses to run  while OpenCode has the DB open (fuser check). Took mine from 1.3 GB to ~578 MB.

Might help others while the upstream fix lands: https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-db-clean

I reproduced the strict-provider replay failure described here and opened #38270 with a targeted fix.

The patch post-processes the final `ModelMessage` list for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`: if an assistant wire message has no non-empty text, it prepends a single-space text part. This covers the aborted `step-start` / reasoning-only shape from this issue, empty-text-only messages, tool-call-only turns, and per-step pieces created after `step-start` splitting without dropping tool-call or reasoning history.

Validation includes 7 regression cases (43/43 tests passing), clean typecheck, and a replay of a previously bricked Kimi K3 session where the follow-up request now succeeds.

This is intentionally broader than #33899: that PR only handles messages with tool calls and therefore leaves this issue's no-tool-call aborted reasoning-only shape unchanged.

Status update from the original patch investigation: PR #33045 was intentionally closed after validation showed that repairing fallback-created session model state was the wrong layer.

The narrower intended direction is to keep provider rate-limit / retry-advisory failures on the original-model retry path and avoid model-replacement fallback for those failures, rather than allowing a fallback model to become durable and repairing session state afterward. The remaining issue is therefore still valid, but #33045 should not be treated as an active fix.

Maintenance update: the linked fix #31052 was automatically closed by the repository's stale-PR cleanup, not because CI or review found a correctness failure. Its compliance and standards checks were green, but it received no maintainer review before cleanup.

The issue remains open and assigned. I am not reopening or replacing the PR automatically because the affected provider-transform area has moved substantially since the original patch and should be revalidated against current `dev` before resubmission.

This looks an NVIDIA compatibility issue. Their /v1/chat/completions endpoint (nemotron-3-ultra-free) intermittently errors on stream_options: { "include_usage": true }. Stripping the field fixes it. 

Adding NVIDIA to a blocklist in the Zen API gateway's modifyBody until NVIDIA resolves it on their end could be temporal fix.

Repro:
curl -X POST https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NVIDIA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
    "stream": true,
    "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}
  }'
Run it a few times — server_error appears intermittently. Remove stream_options and it works consistently.

I put together an opt-in implementation of vertical tabs and opened a PR for it (linked below).

It's fully non-destructive — horizontal tabs remain the default, and it's all behind a **Settings → General → "Vertical tabs"** toggle. Highlights:

- Session tabs move into a resizable sidebar rail, showing full-length titles (the main ask here).
- Collapsible to an icon-only strip with hover-to-reveal.
- Optional **"Tabs on the right"** placement (full left/right mirror).
- The session header is enriched with project name, git branch/worktree, and a working indicator so context isn't lost when tabs are narrow.

### +1 — still affecting OpenCode Go users

I'm running OpenCode Go with Xiaomi MiMo v2.5 as my primary model (via Hermes Agent on a Raspberry Pi). This issue causes intermittent 400 errors whenever a tool result includes image content (vision analysis, browser screenshots, etc.), forcing fallback to non-vision models and breaking my entire image verification workflow.

**What I've tried:**
- Routing through OpenRouter instead of OpenCode Go's native relay (works, but adds latency and loses some features)
- Keeping the fallback chain as a band-aid (all fallback models lack vision, so the system becomes unusable for visual tasks)

PR #32966 by @lexlian looked like the right fix (flatten single-part tool results to plain strings for affected providers), but it was closed by automated cleanup before being reviewed. The fix was tested and passing all 277 tests.

**Request:** Could this be prioritized? The Xiaomi API isn't going to change this behavior — their docs explicitly require string content for tool messages. The relay is the right place to handle this translation.

Happy to help test if a new PR is opened.

Closing after live testing on Bedrock Mantle.

I ran a controlled 4-turn comparison against amazon-bedrock/openai.gpt-5.6-luna:

| Mode | Cumulative input tokens |
|---|---|
| Stateless (store:false, full history) | 1,027 |
| Stateful (store:true, previous_response_id) | 1,282 |

The stateful path was 25% more expensive. previous_response_id saves network bandwidth and request body size, but the Bedrock Mantle endpoint still processes and bills the full conversation context from server-side storage. The input token cost does not decrease.

The issue title claimed this change would reduce per-turn token cost, but the cost is driven by model processing of the full context window, not by network transfer. That cost is invariant regardless of whether the history arrives in the request body or is reconstructed from prior stored state.

The real lever for reducing token cost on Bedrock Mantle is compaction (shrinking what the model needs to process), not previous_response_id chaining. Native compaction via /responses/compact is unavailable through Bedrock, and text-summary compaction is already supported by opencode core.

I tested `previous_response_id` chaining against Bedrock Mantle directly and it does not reduce input token cost.

**Test**: 4-turn conversation, `amazon-bedrock/openai.gpt-5.6-luna`, comparing stateless (store=false, full history each turn) vs stateful (store=true + previous_response_id, delta-only).

| Mode | Cumulative input tokens |
|---|---|
| Stateless (full history re-sent) | 1,027 |
| Stateful (previous_response_id chained) | 1,282 |

Stateful was 25% **more expensive**. The server still processes and bills the full conversation context from server-side storage. previous_response_id saves network bandwidth and request body size, but not token charges.

The cost driver is model processing of the full context window, not network transfer. The real lever is reducing what the model needs to process: compaction. Native compaction via /responses/compact is unavailable through Bedrock. Text-summary compaction already exists in opencode.
